main_text.l: fortuna: de rebus bene praeclareq; gestis:
de honore & dignitate, de affinitate, hisq;
similibus aliis gratulamur: & eidem, aut
usum illorum diuturnum, aut similem in
caeteris quoque successum precamur. Id
quod veri est amici officium: saepe etiam
necessarium, propter homines auctoritate
& potentia magna praeditos: quibus de
aucta dignitate: nominis amplificata glo-
ria: rebus laudabiliter fortiterque admi-
nistratis, gratulari nos oportet. Est autem
diligens in his & accurata primo, cum re-
rum, tum personarum ratio habenda vi-
dendumque sintne ea, propter quae gra-
tulatio instituenda, magna, & apud viros
usurpanda magnos, ideoque amplam, or-
natam, splendidam tractationem requi-
rant: an vero exigua ac minutula, ut qui
splendore in iis, aut ornatu magno uta-
tur, in lente, quod aiunt, unguentum ad-
hibere videatur. Deinde de argumentis
est cogitandum, eademque eo dirigenda:
ut laetitiae nos & gratulationis causas h-
abere iustas appareat. Sumuntur autem il-
la ex causis, effectis, adiunctis, comparatis:
& ostenditur esse ea, quorum gratia ami-
co gratulamur, virtute, consilio, laboribus,
meritis praeclaris: non casu, gratia, pren-
latio-

page.notes: The left margin holds two notes: "In gratulatoriis Epistolis quae confideranda" beside the lines "niftratis" to "rum", where the word "confideranda" is only partly legible, and "Argumenta gratulationum." beside the lines "bere iuftas" to "la ex causis". The second note is not included in the main text above; the transcription keeps only the first note at its place. Long s has been rendered as plain s throughout, following the rules, so "est", "esse", "necessarium" and similar forms read this way. A stray "/" mark appears at the lower right of the text area; it is not printed text and is left out. The catchword "latio-" is a catchword at the right below the last line.
